title: It might not be growing pains
body:
Growing pains don't usually make a kid limp off the field.

If the pain sits at the back of the heel and flares with running, jumping and cleats, it's often Sever's disease, one of the most common causes of heel pain in active kids 8 to 14.

Here's what's happening: 

During a growth spurt the heel bone grows faster than the Achilles tendon can stretch. Until the tendon catches up, it pulls on the growth plate at the back of the heel with every step on the field.

That's why it hurts during game
